A [Letter of Indemnity (LOI)](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/l/letterofindemnity.asp) is a legally binding agreement that guarantees financial protection or compensation to one party if the other party fails to fulfill its contractual obligations.[[1]](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/l/letterofindemnity.asp)[[2]](https://www.ups.com/us/en/supplychain/resources/glossary-term/letter-of-indemnity)

### Key Purposes

- **Risk Mitigation:** Acts as a financial safety net against losses, damages, or breaches of contract.
- **Third-Party Guarantee:** Often issued or backed by banks, insurance companies, or institutions to assure a counterparty that they will be held harmless.
- **Building Trust:** Allows transactions to proceed when standard paperwork or conditions cannot be immediately met.[[1]](https://modaltrans.com/blog/letter-of-indemnity-meaning-uses-legal-implications)[[2]](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/l/letterofindemnity.asp)

### Common Use Cases

- **Shipping and Logistics:** Frequently used to [release cargo without an original Bill of Lading](https://www.ups.com/us/en/supplychain/resources/glossary-term/letter-of-indemnity) , deliver to an alternative port, or handle specialized/unclaimed goods.
- **Borrowing and Leasing:** Protects an owner when a second party borrows valuable equipment, vehicles, or property.
- **Service Contracts:** Assures a client that a contractor's work or liabilities are covered if unexpected issues arise.[[1]](https://www.ups.com/us/en/supplychain/resources/glossary-term/letter-of-indemnity)[[2]](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/l/letterofindemnity.asp)

### Essential Elements of an LOI
A properly executed Letter of Indemnity typically includes:[[1]](https://www.ups.com/us/en/supplychain/resources/glossary-term/letter-of-indemnity)

- **Identified Parties:** Names of the shipper, carrier, receiver, or contracting parties.
- **Detailed Context:** Specific transaction data, shipment details, or the exact obligation being covered.
- **Scope of Liability:** Clear limits on financial responsibility and triggers for compensation.
- **Governing Law:** The legal jurisdiction and venue chosen for resolving disputes.
- **Signatures and Dates:** Formal execution by authorized representatives or supporting institutions.[[1]](https://www.credlix.com/blogs/all-about-letter-of-indemnity-its-meaning-process-sample-format-and-more)[[2]](https://www.ups.com/us/en/supplychain/resources/glossary-term/letter-of-indemnity)

If you are looking to draft or evaluate an LOI, tell me:

- What **type of transaction** or industry is this for (e.g., shipping cargo, equipment rental, service contract)?
- What **specific risk or missing document** are you trying to cover?

expanded_element.snippet: An indemnity obligation is a primary payment obligation, not secondary. A true guarantee contract means the guarantor promises to be responsible if the principal debtor fails to perform their obligations. In a guarantee contract, the guarantor's liability is secondary to the principal debtor's liability.
